_comment: Velthy Party — NestJS. Import: Nests -> Import Egg. The install script runs `npm ci` and `npm run build`, then startup runs the compiled output through startup.mjs. One command only, and one file: startup.mjs starts the server and, when TUNNEL_TOKEN is set, brings cloudflared up as its own child so both live and die together. One instance only: a party lives in the memory of the process holding its WebSockets.
name: Velthy Party (NestJS)
author: velthy@localhost
description: Velthy Listen Together — party server (NestJS). A party is a six-character code, up to five signed-in devices, and one playback state every device re-derives its playhead from. HTTP + WebSocket on one port. Run exactly one instance.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Build the Nest app once, at install time, so the startup command only has to
# run the compiled output.
set -e

cd /mnt/server

echo "--------------------------------------------------"
echo " Velthy Party (NestJS) — installing"
echo "--------------------------------------------------"

echo "Node: $(node --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'missing')"
echo "npm:  $(npm --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'missing')"

echo "Installing dependencies (including dev, needed to build)..."
if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
    npm ci
else
    npm install
fi

echo "Compiling TypeScript..."
npm run build

if [ ! -f dist/bootstrap.js ]; then
    echo "ERROR: dist/bootstrap.js was not produced. Check the build output above."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Pruning dev dependencies from the runtime tree..."
npm prune --omit=dev

echo "--------------------------------------------------"
echo " Install complete."
echo " Startup runs: node startup.mjs (uses dist/)"
echo " Port: ${SERVER_PORT}"
echo "   http  http://<host>:${SERVER_PORT}/api/time"
echo "   ws    ws://<host>:${SERVER_PORT}/ws/parties/{code}?token=..."
echo "--------------------------------------------------"

variables.name: Server port
variables.description: Port the process listens on. Must match one of the ports the host allocates (this deployment: 33183 / 37720 / 25620) and the tunnel's Public Hostname service in the Cloudflare dashboard. The server reads PORT then SERVER_PORT, falling back to 8080.

variables.name: Node environment
variables.description: Leave as production. Development adds verbose logging.

variables.name: Max members
variables.description: Devices allowed in one party. Counted in devices, not people: one account on a phone and a tablet is two.

variables.name: State heartbeat (ms)
variables.description: How often the server re-states playback state to everyone, unprompted.

variables.name: Play lead (ms)
variables.description: How far ahead a resume is scheduled, giving every device one common instant to aim at.

variables.name: Disconnect grace (ms)
variables.description: How long a dropped socket keeps its slot. Phones lose WebSockets in tunnels and on screen-off.

variables.name: Empty party TTL (ms)
variables.description: How long a party with nobody in it is held before its code and memory are reclaimed.

variables.name: Party max age (ms)
variables.description: Hard ceiling on any one party's life, regardless of activity.

variables.name: Control rate per second
variables.description: Token-bucket ceiling on control frames one member may send.

variables.name: Max queue length
variables.description: Bounds the queue one member can hand the server to hold and rebroadcast.

variables.name: Allowed origins
variables.description: Comma-separated browser origins allowed to open a socket, or * for any. Empty allows any, which is correct for the Android app (no Origin header).

variables.name: Cloudflare Tunnel token
variables.description: Optional. Paste the tunnel token from Cloudflare Zero Trust (Networks -> Tunnels -> Cloudflared) to expose this server over HTTPS/WSS with no port forwarding. When set, startup.mjs starts cloudflared itself as a child process, so ONE command runs both. Leave empty to serve locally without a tunnel. The token is a credential: keep it secret, and set the public hostname in the dashboard to point at localhost:<port> (the same port as SERVER_PORT).

variables.name: Update from git
variables.description: Set to 1 and the server updates ITSELF at startup: it fetches the branch below, checks the new commit out, reinstalls if the lockfile moved, and rebuilds. Without this, a restart runs the code on disk (and rebuilds dist/ if src/ is newer) but never fetches anything new. The log says which happened.

variables.name: Repository URL
variables.description: Only needed once, on a server whose files were uploaded rather than cloned: the server sets up .git itself and follows this repository from then on. .env and node_modules are never touched by an update.

variables.name: Git branch
variables.description: The branch the server follows when updating from git.
